/-!
# Carathéodory conjecture

The **Carathéodory conjecture** states that any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface
in three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points, i.e. points at which
the two principal curvatures coincide (equivalently, the second fundamental form is a scalar
multiple of the first fundamental form).

A closed convex surface is modelled as the boundary $\partial K$ of a compact convex body
$K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior. The surface is $C^2$ when it is locally a
regular level set of a $C^2$ function $F$; a point $p$ of such a surface is umbilical when the
Hessian of $F$ at $p$, restricted to the tangent plane $\ker dF_p$, is a scalar multiple of the
inner product. This is the classical notion: the second fundamental form at $p$ is
$-\mathrm{Hess}\,F_p / \|\nabla F(p)\|$ on the tangent plane, for any local defining function
$F$. Flat points (both principal curvatures zero) count as umbilical.

The conjecture is known for real-analytic surfaces (Hamburger). Guilfoyle and Klingenberg
have claimed a proof for $C^{3,\alpha}$ surfaces, and Alpöge has announced a $C^\infty$
counterexample; the conjecture is currently listed as open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Carathéodory conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carath%C3%A9odory_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- M. Ghomi, R. Howard, *Normal curvatures of asymptotically constant graphs and Carathéodory's
  conjecture*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 140 (2012), [arXiv:1101.3031](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.3031)
- B. Guilfoyle, W. Klingenberg, *Proof of the Carathéodory conjecture*,
  [arXiv:0808.0851](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0851)
-/

structure IsLocalDefiningFunction (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) (F : ℝ³ → ℝ) : Prop where
  contDiffAt : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p
  fderiv_ne_zero : fderiv ℝ F p ≠ 0
  eventually_mem_iff : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 p, x ∈ S ↔ F x = 0
blocks.docstring:
`F` is a *local $C^2$ defining function* for the set `S ⊆ ℝ³` at the point `p`: `F` is twice

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's IsImmersion / IsImmersionAt (Geometry/Manifold/Immersion.lean) and ContMDiff on the sphere manifold; these describe maps, not subsets of ℝ³, carry no C² submanifold-of-ℝ³ API and no second fundamental form, so a level-set description was used instead. justification.why_needed: Expresses that a set S ⊆ ℝ³ is, near a point p, the regular zero set of a function F that is C² near p (ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p, fderiv ℝ F p ≠ 0, and x ∈ S ↔ F x = 0 eventually near p). def IsC2Surface (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ S, ∃ F : ℝ³ → ℝ, IsLocalDefiningFunction S p F
blocks.docstring:
A set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is a *$C^2$ surface* (an embedded, twice continuously differentiable surface)
if near each of its points it is a regular level set of a $C^2$ function.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsManifold / ChartedSpace structures in Mathlib apply to abstract types, not to subsets of ℝ³ with the induced geometry; no Mathlib predicate for 'C² embedded surface in ℝ³' exists.
justification.name: CaratheodoryConjecture.IsC2Surface
justification.why_needed: S ⊆ ℝ³ is a C² (twice continuously differentiable, embedded) surface: every point of S admits a local C² defining function. This is the standard regular-level-set characterisation, equivalent to local C² graphs by the implicit function theorem.

def IsUmbilicalPoint (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) : Prop :=
  p ∈ S ∧ ∃ F : ℝ³ → ℝ, IsLocalDefiningFunction S p F ∧ ∃ κ : ℝ,
    ∀ v w : ℝ³, fderiv ℝ F p v = 0 → fderiv ℝ F p w = 0 →
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) p v w = κ * ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ
blocks.docstring:
A point `p` of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is an *umbilical point* of `S` if `S` has a local $C^2$ defining
function `F` at `p` whose Hessian at `p`, restricted to the tangent plane $\ker dF_p$, is a scalar
multiple `κ` of the inner product. Since the second fundamental form of a $C^2$ surface at `p` is
$-\mathrm{Hess}\,F_p / \|\nabla F(p)\|$ on the tangent plane, this says exactly that the two
principal curvatures of `S` at `p` coincide (including the case where both vanish).

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for umbilic / SecondFundamental / principal curvature / shape operator / Weingarten / mean curvature: nothing exists. Mathlib's fderiv/ContDiffAt were used as the underlying primitives.
justification.name: CaratheodoryConjecture.IsUmbilicalPoint
justification.why_needed: p ∈ S is umbilical iff for some local C² defining function F at p there is κ with D²F_p(v,w) = κ⟪v,w⟫ for all v,w in the tangent plane ker dF_p. Since the second fundamental form of a C² surface is −Hess F|_T/‖∇F‖ for any defining function F, this is exactly 'both principal curvatures coincide' (flat points included). Mathlib has no second fundamental form, shape operator, principal curvatures or umbilics.

blocks.name: IsUmbilicalPoint
blocks.text:
/-- A point `p` of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is an *umbilical point* of `S` if `S` has a local $C^2$ defining
function `F` at `p` whose Hessian at `p`, restricted to the tangent plane $\ker dF_p$, is a scalar

@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isLocalDefiningFunction_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsLocalDefiningFunction (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p (fun x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) where
  contDiffAt := ((contDiff_id.norm_sq ℝ).sub contDiff_const).contDiffAt
  fderiv_ne_zero := by
    have h : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ³ ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) p = 2 • innerSL ℝ p :=
      ((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq p).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv
    rw [h]
    intro h0
    have := congrArg (fun L : ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℝ ↦ L p) h0
    simp [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp hp] at this
  eventually_mem_iff := Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ by
    simp [sub_eq_zero, pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg x) two_ne_zero]

@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isUmbilicalPoint_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsUmbilicalPoint (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p := by
  refine ⟨hp, _, isLocalDefiningFunction_sphere p hp, 2, fun v w _ _ ↦ ?_⟩
  have h : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ³ ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) = fun x ↦ (2 • innerSL ℝ) x := by
    ext x : 1
    exact ((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq x).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv
  rw [h, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv]
  simp

claims.decomposer_note: Single global assertion: for every compact convex body in ℝ³ with nonempty interior whose boundary is a C² (twice continuously differentiable, the minimal regularity for umbilics to be well-defined per the article and Ghomi–Howard's C² formulation) embedded surface, the set of umbilical points (points where the two principal curvatures coincide, i.e. the second fundamental form is a scalar multiple of the first — flat points κ₁=κ₂=0 included, since only 'convex', not 'strictly convex' as in Guilfoyle–Klingenberg, is assumed) has cardinality at least two, counted as distinct points, not with index/multiplicity; the formalizer must supply the umbilic definition (absent from Mathlib) and keep the category `research open` despite the article's mention of an announced C^∞ counterexample.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and state mathematically equivalent, faithful propositions: K ⊆ ℝ³ compact convex with nonempty interior (Ghomi–Howard's 'closed convex surface' = boundary of a compact convex set with interior points), frontier K a C² embedded surface, conclusion two distinct umbilical points (no index/multiplicity), umbilic = second fundamental form proportional to first with the scalar allowed to be 0 (flat points included). c01 was chosen as the cleanest: local defining functions via ContDiffAt ℝ 2 + nonzero derivative + eventual agreement of the zero set; umbilic = Hessian restricted to ker dF_p equals κ·⟪·,·⟫ (correct since II = −Hess F|_T/‖∇F‖ for any C² defining function, so the ∃F form is independent of F; Hessian is the true second derivative because F is C² near p, and symmetric so the bilinear form is equivalent to the quadratic/principal-curvature form). It uses the repo's ℝ³ notation, binder-style hypotheses, ascending AMS 52 53, full module docstring with references, and fully proved `category test` lemmas showing the unit ball satisfies the hypotheses and the sphere is everywhere umbilical, which guards against vacuity/junk values in the bespoke definitions. Shipped verbatim (no edits needed).

context:
In differential geometry, the Carathéodory conjecture is a mathematical conjecture attributed to Constantin Carathéodory by Hans Ludwig Hamburger, stating that any convex, closed and sufficiently smooth surface in three dimensional Euclidean space must admit at least two umbilic points. 
Much of the early work on the conjecture concerned the real-analytic case. Beginning with Hamburger's work, several proofs and revisions were subsequently given by Gerrit Bol, Tilla Klotz and Charles J. Titus.. Klotz identified a gap in Bol's proof, while Hanspeter Scherbel later argued that the proofs of Klotz and Titus also contained gaps.
In the more general smooth case, however, Levent Alpöge announced in August 2026 an explicit $C^{\infty }$ counterexample checked with John-Paul Smith and Anthropic's artificial-intelligence system Claude.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (compact convex body with nonempty interior, C² boundary, umbilic = second fundamental form proportional to the first with flat points included, distinct points not counted with index, category research open) were followed exactly.

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry InnerProductSpace

namespace CaratheodoryConjecture

/-- `F` is a *local $C^2$ defining function* for the set `S ⊆ ℝ³` at the point `p`: `F` is twice
continuously differentiable near `p`, its derivative at `p` is nonzero (so its zero set is a
regular surface near `p`), and `S` coincides with the zero set of `F` in a neighbourhood of `p`. -/
structure IsLocalDefiningFunction (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) (F : ℝ³ → ℝ) : Prop where
  contDiffAt : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p
  fderiv_ne_zero : fderiv ℝ F p ≠ 0
  eventually_mem_iff : ∀ᶠ x in 𝓝 p, x ∈ S ↔ F x = 0

/-- A set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is a *$C^2$ surface* (an embedded, twice continuously differentiable surface)
if near each of its points it is a regular level set of a $C^2$ function. -/
def IsC2Surface (S : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∀ p ∈ S, ∃ F : ℝ³ → ℝ, IsLocalDefiningFunction S p F

/-- A point `p` of a set `S ⊆ ℝ³` is an *umbilical point* of `S` if `S` has a local $C^2$ defining
function `F` at `p` whose Hessian at `p`, restricted to the tangent plane $\ker dF_p$, is a scalar
multiple `κ` of the inner product. Since the second fundamental form of a $C^2$ surface at `p` is
$-\mathrm{Hess}\,F_p / \|\nabla F(p)\|$ on the tangent plane, this says exactly that the two
principal curvatures of `S` at `p` coincide (including the case where both vanish). -/
def IsUmbilicalPoint (S : Set ℝ³) (p : ℝ³) : Prop :=
  p ∈ S ∧ ∃ F : ℝ³ → ℝ, IsLocalDefiningFunction S p F ∧ ∃ κ : ℝ,
    ∀ v w : ℝ³, fderiv ℝ F p v = 0 → fderiv ℝ F p w = 0 →
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) p v w = κ * ⟪v, w⟫_ℝ

/-- The function $x \mapsto \|x\|^2 - 1$ is a local defining function for the unit sphere at each
of its points. -/
@[category test, AMS 53]
theorem isLocalDefiningFunction_sphere (p : ℝ³) (hp : p ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :
    IsLocalDefiningFunction (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) p (fun x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) where
  contDiffAt := ((contDiff_id.norm_sq ℝ).sub contDiff_const).contDiffAt

    have h : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ³ ↦ ‖x‖ ^ 2 - 1) p = 2 • innerSL ℝ p :=

    intro h0
    have := congrArg (fun L : ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℝ ↦ L p) h0
    simp [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp hp] at this
  eventually_mem_iff := Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x ↦ by
    simp [sub_eq_zero, pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg x) two_ne_zero]

theorem isC2Surface_sphere : IsC2Surface (Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1) :=

    ext x : 1
    exact ((hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq x).hasFDerivAt.sub_const 1).fderiv
  rw [h, ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv]

/--
**Carathéodory conjecture.** Any convex, closed and twice-differentiable surface in
three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points.

Precisely: let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact convex set with nonempty interior whose
boundary $\partial K$ is a $C^2$ surface. Then $\partial K$ has at least two distinct umbilical
points, i.e. points at which the two principal curvatures coincide.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52 53]
theorem caratheodory_conjecture (K : Set ℝ³) (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hKc : IsCompact K)
    (hKi : (interior K).Nonempty) (hS : IsC2Surface (frontier K)) :
    ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) p ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) q := by
  sorry

end CaratheodoryConjecture

items: 'Convex, closed surface' is modelled as the boundary `frontier K` of a compact convex set K ⊆ ℝ³ with nonempty interior (as prescribed by the decomposition table). The nonempty-interior hypothesis is essential: for K = ∅ the frontier is empty, `IsC2Surface ∅` holds vacuously and the conclusion would be false; degenerate lower-dimensional convex sets are also excluded. Strict convexity is NOT assumed (only 'convex' in the statement), so flat pieces are allowed.

'Twice-differentiable' is formalised as C² (ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p for a local defining function), following the decomposition table and Ghomi–Howard's C² formulation, rather than mere twice-differentiability without continuity of the second derivative.

The surface regularity is expressed via local regular level sets (IsLocalDefiningFunction) rather than local graphs after a rigid motion or a C² embedding of S²; these are all equivalent for embedded C² surfaces (implicit function theorem), and the level-set form avoids coordinate bookkeeping. ContDiffAt (C² on some neighbourhood of p) is used rather than global ContDiff; the two are equivalent by cutting off with a bump function.

Umbilic is defined as: the Hessian fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) p of a local defining function F, restricted to the tangent plane ker (fderiv ℝ F p), equals κ·⟪·,·⟫ for some real κ. For a C² surface this is independent of the choice of F (if G is another defining function then dG_p = c·dF_p and Hess G|_T = c·Hess F|_T), and equals the classical condition κ₁ = κ₂ because II = −Hess F|_T/‖∇F‖. The definition uses ∃ F (a witness) rather than ∀ F, which avoids vacuous truth at non-C² points; both readings coincide on C² surfaces. The sign convention is irrelevant since κ is existentially quantified. Flat points (κ = 0) count as umbilical, consistent with the table.
'At least two umbilical points' is formalised as ∃ p q, p ≠ q ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) p ∧ IsUmbilicalPoint (frontier K) q — distinct points, no index/multiplicity counting.

Category kept as `research open` per the task despite the Wikipedia article's mention of an announced C^∞ counterexample (Alpöge) and a claimed C^{3,α} proof (Guilfoyle–Klingenberg); the module docstring records these as claims/announcements only.

Three `category test` theorems (with proofs) check the definitions on the unit sphere: ‖x‖²−1 is a local defining function, the sphere is a C² surface, and every point of the sphere is umbilical (κ = 2). These show the hypotheses of the conjecture are satisfiable and the umbilic notion is not vacuous.

reviewer_notes: Original statement is informal ('twice-differentiable'); following the decomposition notes and Ghomi–Howard (arXiv:1101.3031) it is formalised as C² (ContDiffAt ℝ 2), not merely twice differentiable. Only convexity (not strict convexity) is assumed, so flat points (κ₁=κ₂=0) count as umbilics, consistent with the notes. Category kept `research open` despite the article's mention of an announced C^∞ counterexample (Alpöge) and the Guilfoyle–Klingenberg claimed proof; the module docstring records these as claims only. Candidate comparison: c04/c08 (level sets on an explicit open set, c08 via ConvexBody + iteratedFDeriv), c05/c07 (level sets, ∀-style statement, weaker docstrings, c07 introduces a global abbrev `E`), c03/c06 (regular C² parametrisations with IsEmbedding and everywhere-injective derivative; c03 concludes via encard ≥ 2) are all faithful alternatives. c02's chart notion only requires injective derivative at the base parameter and injectivity (not embedding) of the chart, which in general admits non-embedded 'figure-6' surfaces; for frontier K (a topological 2-sphere) it is still equivalent by invariance of domain, but it is the weakest definition and was not chosen. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised.
statement: Carathéodory conjecture: any convex, closed, and twice-differentiable surface in three-dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilical points.
